I've been farming this ground for 30 years, so I mostly do what worked last year and adjust a little. 12 mu is not small, not big — enough that I have to think carefully about what I spend on fertilizer and spray.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use an improved variety — the seed shop in town sells Jimai or Shimai types, most neighbors plant those and get good wheat. Before planting I plough once with the tractor service, then rotary to make the seedbed smooth. Base fertilizer I put down compound 15-15-15, about 3 bags (50 kg each) per mu split across the field — that gives me roughly 22-23 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K. Then at jointing (around March) I top-dress urea, maybe 15 kg per mu, so total N comes to about 28 kg. Wheat here needs water — I irrigate 4 times from my well: before winter, at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling. I spray 3 times: once for weeds in spring, once for aphids and powdery mildew, once at heading for scab and pests together. I expect about 480 kg per mu — last few years have been like that.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no-till directly into the stubble with the seed drill service. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Denghai type — everyone uses hybrids for summer maize now. Fertilizer I use compound at planting, about 2 bags per mu, then top-dress urea at big trumpet stage around 15 kg. Total N about 23 kg. Summer rain usually enough but I give one irrigation if July is dry. Spray twice — once for borer at whorl stage, once if armyworm shows up. Expect around 580 kg per mu.
